question: is env_params' daylight-saving error in the LABEL only, or in the DATA?
conclusion: DATA SHIFTED -- env_params computes on STANDARD time (EST, -05:00) even on dates when the AOI is on daylight time (EDT, -04:00)

decisive_evidence.method: clear-sky GHI is pure astronomy, no weather noise. Its peak must fall at true solar noon.
decisive_evidence.solar_algorithm: verified to 0.0 deg against a known value in N-33

inconclusive_attempts.why_they_failed: env_params RH is a modelled field whose diurnal phase does not track a station 8 km away closely enough; the correlation curve is too flat near its peak to locate a 1-hour shift regardless of sample size

consequence: a caller requesting 12:00 on a summer day receives the conditions for 12:00 EST = 13:00 EDT, i.e. one hour LATER in true local time than requested

affects_our_work.N-33 stability: NOT affected -- used ASOS wind and our own solar calculation, not env_params timing
affects_our_work.N-25 sharpening / N-26 coverage: NOT affected -- both use heatmap, and forecast and outcome are requested with the SAME window specification, so any systematic offset cancels
affects_our_work.N-31 wind alignment: potentially misaligned by up to 1 h against ASOS, but its conclusion rests on the single-template finding which does not depend on wind timing
affects_our_work.open: whether heatmap is ALSO on EST cannot be distinguished by the horizon test -- both readings fit the 12 h cut. Our tests are self-consistent either way.

secondary_finding: with a multi-hour window, env_params returns ARRAYS for parameters (24 values) but a SCALAR for solar_irradiance -- inconsistent, and it blocked the array version of this test
